*** SPRINT 75 / V0.29.30: 4 of 11 closed, 3 PASSING (US-561, US-563, US-566), 1 blocked-by-hardware (US-560/BL-034). NEXT ITERATION PICKS UP US-564 (plausibility gate, size L) per the fixed closeout order -- nothing blocks it. US-565 follows it, THEN the F-132 chrome stories (US-555..559). ***

*** US-566 CLOSED passes:true -- powerwatch must log its arm decision. Full AC-by-AC detail in sprint.json completionNotes; reusable lessons below. ***

RE-MEASURING THE PREMISE IS NOW 4 SPRINTS RUNNING, AND THIS TIME IT NARROWED THE DEFECT RATHER THAN WIDENING IT. AC-1 asserted 'eclipse-powerwatch emits ZERO application log lines today'. **That is FALSE, and one journalctl settled it in seconds.** The unit's journal is full of application lines -- the GPIO6 power-LOST trigger, the boot-grace 'ignoring' lines, UpsMonitor I2C warnings -- all from the same pids. What it has ZERO of, across 8 service starts, is the arm-SUCCESS line. **Real mechanism: the module never configured logging at all, so logging.lastResort (level WARNING, stderr) was the only sink and the ENTIRE INFO TIER went on the floor.** The success line was INFO (invisible); the failure line is ERROR (visible, never fired). GENERALISE: US-560's premise was refuted, US-561's and US-563's were confirmed-and-widened, US-566's was confirmed-but-narrowed. All four were cheap to check and all four changed the build.

**A PREMISE THAT IS TOO BROAD IS AS COSTLY AS ONE THAT IS WRONG.** Building to 'zero log lines' would have sent me hunting for missing log calls -- and there are none, both branches were already unconditional. A reviewer reading the cited lines 439-456 finds nothing wrong, because the defect is in what is NOT there (no basicConfig/setupLogging anywhere in this module's graph). When a story says 'X never happens', ask WHICH X and check the neighbours: the neighbours working is the clue.

**SILENCE THAT MEANS TWO THINGS IS NOT AN INSTRUMENT.** Absence of the arm ERROR meant EITHER 'armed fine' OR 'logging is broken', with nothing to distinguish them -- the same false-healthy shape US-561 removed from the kiosk watchdog ONE STORY EARLIER in this sprint. Whenever a good-news path is silent by design, the bad-news path cannot be trusted either. Fix is to make the GOOD news explicit, not to add more failure logging.

**DO NOT PIN A SAFETY FACT TO A TIER A CONFIG CHANGE CAN SILENCE.** The arm decision is emitted at WARNING (armed) / ERROR (not-armed), not INFO, and I pinned the FLOOR (levelno >= WARNING) rather than the exact level, with the reason in the docstring. It fires once per service start so severity costs no journal volume. Defence in depth BEHIND the setupLogging fix, not instead of it -- if logging config ever regresses to lastResort again, the decision still gets through. Both branches carry one greppable prefix so ONE command answers the operator's question: `journalctl -u eclipse-powerwatch.service --grep='ARM DECISION'`.

**VERIFY YOUR DISCRIMINATOR IS NOT VACUOUS BEFORE TRUSTING A GREEN.** My unit tests would only have gone red pre-change in the useless ImportError way. The load-bearing guard is in the systemd-parity SUBPROCESS (the only test that runs real main() wiring), asserting (a) the logger NAME appears -> a configured handler, not lastResort, and (b) '| INFO' appears -> the level filter admits INFO. I proved both were genuinely red pre-change with a 10-second scratch probe: **with no handlers, lastResort emits a BARE message -- no level name, no logger name -- and drops INFO entirely.** That probe also independently corroborated the live-Pi journal. Same lesson as US-563's negative self-test: a guard never SEEN to fail is not known to be a guard.

**WHEN YOU REWRITE THE ONLY DIAGNOSTIC LINE ON A PATH, PIN WHAT IT USED TO CARRY.** The old ERROR carried 6 remediation facts (REFUSING to arm / OBD collector / NOTHING will be powered off / pi.powerWatch.pldGpioPin / pldPowerPresentHigh / redeploy). A parametrised MOVED-pin test asserts all 6 survive the rewrite. Adding a prefix while quietly dropping the remediation would have passed every other test I wrote.

FIXED A SMALL SSOT LEAK INSIDE THE LINES I WAS ALREADY REPLACING (not scope creep -- it was the exact expression under edit): the old ERROR read diagnostics from raw `pld.*` while the decision came from `provider.startupArmCheck()`. Two acquisition sites for one fact = the one place the explanation can disagree with the decision it explains. Evidence now reads through the PowerSourceProvider SSOT.

ALSO WORTH KNOWING: a disarmed powerwatch is `systemctl is-active` == active and otherwise SILENT, so it looks exactly like a protected one. The old failure branch was a bare `threading.Event().wait()` -- announce once, then nothing, and that line ages out of the journal. Now it re-states its cause on an interval.

HONEST BOUND I FLAGGED RATHER THAN BURIED: `setupLogging()` sets the ROOT level and CLEARS root handlers, so third-party INFO in this process's graph now reaches the journal too. Steady state is quiet (smbus2 no logging; urllib3/SyncClient only inside a shutdown window; UpsMonitor already WARNING), so ~one extra startup line -- but it IS a behaviour change to a shutdown-critical service. Worth a glance at journal volume on first deploy.

OWED AT DEPLOY, NOT CLAIMED: validationCriteria #1 needs the code deployed + the Pi rebooted (deploy is PM's). **PM: after deploying V0.29.30 run `journalctl -u eclipse-powerwatch.service --grep='ARM DECISION' --no-pager` -- exactly one line per boot. If it reads NOT-ARMED, that is the finding the CIO's X1209 hold-up investigation has been missing.**

ENVIRONMENT (re-confirmed this session): Pi reachable via `ssh -o BatchMode=yes chi-eclipse-01`; **a `;`-separated compound DOES work when it is inside the quoted ssh argument** (the Bash tool's compound refusal applies to the local command line, not the remote string) -- handy for `systemctl show` + `is-active` in one call. **Bash output redirection is confined to the working dirs: `> _file.txt` from the default cwd works, an absolute `/z/o/...` path is REFUSED.** `python -m pytest <dir>` without `-q` DOES print the 'N passed' summary -- use it and skip the redirect dance. `python -m ruff check <files>` for lint (`make` is not on PATH and exits 127, which reads like a pass). Scratch files must live in the repo and be rm'd before committing. `git commit -F - <<'EOF'` heredoc works cleanly. Index lock CLEAR all session.
